sample.question: What is the primary ordering principle of a queue?
sample.answer: A queue follows first in, first out (FIFO) ordering.
sample.sourceQuote: A queue follows first in, first out (FIFO) ordering.

sample.question: What happens when the Aster queue is full?
sample.answer: The enqueue operation rejects the new item and preserves all existing items.
sample.sourceQuote: When the Aster queue is full, enqueue rejects the new item and preserves all existing items.

sample.question: How does a circular buffer handle index wrapping?
sample.answer: It uses (index + 1) modulo capacity to advance the index.
sample.sourceQuote: Advancing an index uses (index + 1) modulo capacity.

sample.question: Which data structure follows a last in, first out (LIFO) ordering principle?
sample.explanation: A stack follows LIFO ordering, meaning the most recently added item is the first one removed, unlike a queue which follows FIFO.
sample.sourceQuote: A stack instead follows last in, first out (LIFO) ordering.

sample.question: What is the name of the diagnostic code used when the Aster queue is full?
sample.explanation: The document explicitly states that the overflow diagnostic code for the Aster queue is ZEPHYR-47, which is returned when the queue is full.
sample.sourceQuote: Its overflow diagnostic code is ZEPHYR-47.

sample.question: How does a circular buffer handle index advancement when it reaches the end of the array?
options: It stops at the last index
It wraps around to the beginning
sample.correctAnswer: It wraps around to the beginning
sample.explanation: A circular buffer uses modulo arithmetic to wrap indices around, allowing the head and tail pointers to reuse the fixed-size array without shifting data.
sample.sourceQuote: Advancing an index uses (index + 1) modulo capacity.
